permutationLabel: Incidental finding — 12 mm gallbladder polyp alongside gallstones
summary: 56-year-old man with typical biliary colic; ultrasound shows gallstones and an incidental 12 mm sessile gallbladder polyp. Normal bloods.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Episodes of right upper abdominal pain after meals
inputs.hpi: Three episodes in two months of right upper quadrant pain after meals lasting a few hours, with nausea; settles fully. No fever, jaundice or weight loss. Ultrasound shows gallstones and a 12 mm polyp in the gallbladder.

exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender at rest. No mass.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Several mobile gallstones. Separate 12 mm sessile, non-mobile, non-shadowing polyp on the fundal wall with internal vascularity. Wall otherwise 2 mm. CBD 5 mm. Liver normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Biliary colic with a 12 mm gallbladder polyp
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Symptomatic cholelithiasis (biliary colic) with an incidental 12 mm sessile gallbladder polyp.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: adaptiveTriage emergency_now (score 125) for a pain-free outpatient: "No fever, jaundice or weight loss" fires biliary-obstruction and malignancy rules.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts: replace the substring helpers exam()/hasSx()/hasRadResult() and hasFever (which matches "temp" and "afebrile") with a negation-aware matcher (NegEx-style: no/not/without/denies/negative/absent within ~5 tokens) and read fever from the temperature vital (≥38 °C), not from text.

redFlags.note: A polyp ≥10 mm carries a malignancy risk and changes the indication/urgency and the histology plan.
redFlags.knownGapNote: No engine mentions the 12 mm polyp (no polyp rule in triage, prompts or protocols).
redFlags.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts: add a radiology-result prompt for gallbladder polyp with size parsing (≥10 mm → cholecystectomy if fit; 6–9 mm → surveillance; ESGAR/EAES/EFISDS/ESGE 2022).

mustInclude.note: Two independent indications: symptomatic gallstones and a polyp ≥10 mm. Critical because a missed polyp-driven cholecystectomy risks a missed gallbladder cancer.
The specimen must be reviewed histologically (polyp ≥10 mm).

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: ESGAR/EAES/EFISDS/ESGE joint guideline — management and follow-up of gallbladder polyps (update)
guideline.section: Cholecystectomy for polyps ≥10 mm (if fit), and for polyps with gallbladder symptoms; histology of the specimen
guideline.citation: Foley KG, Lahaye MJ, Thoeni RF, et al. Eur Radiol. 2022;32:3358–3368.

guideline.name: NICE CG188 — Gallstone disease: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Asymptomatic gallbladder stones in a normal gallbladder and biliary tree: reassure, no treatment; symptomatic gallbladder stones: offer laparoscopic cholecystectomy; LFTs and ultrasound for suspected gallstone disease
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG188, October 2014.

rationale: Permutation: same presentation plus an incidental 12 mm gallbladder polyp. Tests whether the engines surface the polyp (malignancy risk) and keep cholecystectomy with histology in the plan; no engine is expected to know gallbladder polyp thresholds today.
